title: Distributed Consistency Models
intro: Consistency models specify the contract between a distributed storage system and its clients regarding the ordering and visibility of concurrent data mutations.
objectives: Classify consistency spectrum from Linearizability to Eventual Consistency.
Implement Read-Your-Writes and Monotonic Reads in distributed architectures.
Differentiate Strong Eventual Consistency (CRDTs) from Last-Write-Wins (LWW).
body:
### The Consistency Spectrum

1. **Linearizability (Strong Consistency)**: Operations take effect instantaneously at a discrete point in time between their invocation and response. Looks like a single global register.
2. **Sequential Consistency**: Operations appear in some global sequential order that is consistent with the program order on each individual node.
3. **Causal Consistency**: Causally related operations must be seen by all nodes in the same order. Concurrent, un-related operations can be seen in different orders.
4. **Read-Your-Writes**: A client that executes an update will always immediately observe that update on subsequent reads.
5. **Eventual Consistency**: If no new updates are made, all replicas will eventually converge to the same value.
keyIdea: Linearizability requires synchronous multi-node coordination. Weaker models (Causal, Read-Your-Writes) deliver massive throughput gains with acceptable domain trade-offs.

concepts.title: Vector Clocks
concepts.body: Arrays of logical counters capturing causal relationships between distributed concurrent mutations.

concepts.title: Sticky Routing
concepts.body: Routing a client's read queries to the same replica or master for 10 seconds after a write ensures Read-Your-Writes.

examples: Amazon cart (dynamo eventual consistency with shopping cart merging).

quiz.prompt: Which consistency guarantee ensures a user always sees their own comment immediately after posting it?
quiz.explanation: Read-Your-Writes guarantees that a specific client always observes its own preceding writes.
